--- You use OpenCode on more than one computer, and every machine drifts: a new agent here, an MCP server there, a skill you installed on the laptop and forgot on the desktop. **opencode-github-sync** keeps all of them on one setup through a private GitHub repository. Run it by hand when you want, or let your everyday machines sync themselves in the background. It works with OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2, and both can share the same repository. **What you get** - Config, instruction files, agents, commands, plugins, themes and skills on every machine. - Optionally your logins and your recent conversations, too. - Settings that belong to one machine stay on that machine. - Nothing is overwritten without a copy kept first, and a broken sync can be repaired from the command line even when OpenCode will not start. ## Contents - [Install](#install) - [First run](#first-run) - [What gets synced](#what-gets-synced) - [OpenCode 2](#opencode-2) - [Autosync](#autosync) - [Per-machine overrides](#per-machine-overrides) - [Sessions](#sessions) - [Credentials](#credentials) - [Safety](#safety) - [The menu](#the-menu) - [OpenCode plugin](#opencode-plugin) - [Commands](#commands) - [Settings file](#settings-file) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [Upgrading](#upgrading) - [Development](#development) --- ## Install **macOS / Linux** ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lazyalex616/opencode-github-sync/main/install.sh | sh ``` **Windows** (PowerShell 5.1 or 7) ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lazyalex616/opencode-github-sync/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` The installer checks for Node.js 18+ and git. If one is missing it shows the command that would install it and asks before running anything. Then it runs `npm install -g opencode-github-sync@latest` and opens the menu. Already have Node.js? This does the same: ```bash npm install -g opencode-github-sync opencode-sync ``` **Requirements** | | Needed for | | --- | --- | | Node.js 18 or newer | everything | | Node.js 22.5 or newer | sessions, and credentials on OpenCode 2 (they use Node's built-in SQLite) | | git | everything | | GitHub CLI (`gh`), signed in | only `init`, which creates the repository for you | | OpenCode 1.3.4+ or 2.x | the optional plugin | ### Set up a machine in one line Pass options to skip every question, for example when preparing a new machine: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lazyalex616/opencode-github-sync/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --mode auto --repo you/my-opencode-config ``` ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lazyalex616/opencode-github-sync/main/install.ps1))) -Mode auto -Repo you/my-opencode-config ``` | Option | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `--mode cli` | Install the command only | | `--mode link` | Link `--repo` and sync once | | `--mode auto` | Link, sync once and turn on autosync | | `--repo owner/name` | The repository (a git URL works too); created as private if it does not exist | | `--interval N` | Autosync every N minutes (minimum 2, default 5) | | `--lang en` / `zh-CN` | Interface language | | `--proxy URL` | Proxy for npm and git, during install and for later syncs | | `--yes` | Install a missing Node.js or git without asking | | `--package SPEC` | npm package spec to install (default `opencode-github-sync@latest`) | | `--dry-run` | Print what would run, change nothing | On Windows each option is the same word with one leading dash: `-Mode`, `-Repo`, `-Interval`, `-Lang`, `-Proxy`, `-Yes`, `-Package`, `-DryRun`. --- ## First run

The first time you run `opencode-sync` it asks how this machine should work: | | Command only | Primary device + autosync | | --- | --- | --- | | How it syncs | You run `opencode-sync push` / `pull`, or the plugin pulls when OpenCode starts | The operating system syncs every few minutes, even while OpenCode is closed | | Good for | A machine you use now and then, a shared or locked-down machine | The machines you work on every day | | Background job | None | Task Scheduler, launchd or a systemd timer | Then it links a repository: - **No repository yet?** It creates a private one with `gh` (or run `opencode-sync init`). - **Already have one?** Pick it from the list, or give `owner/name` or any git URL (or run `opencode-sync link owner/name`). If the repository already has content and this machine has its own files, the menu shows the differences and lets you pick a side. The losing side's files are copied to the [recovery folder](#safety) first. You can change your mind any time under **Autosync**. Autosync is per machine: turning it on here never turns it on anywhere else. --- ## What gets synced

Your `~/.config/opencode` folder becomes a working copy of the repository. Everything that lives elsewhere is mirrored into a folder inside it. | On your machine | In the repository | What it holds | | --- | --- | --- | | `~/.config/opencode/` | the root | `opencode.json(c)`, `tui.json(c)`, OpenCode 2's `cli.json`, agents, commands, plugins, themes, instruction files | | `~/.local/share/opencode/` | `_data/` | project metadata; logins if you [opt in](#credentials) | | `~/.local/state/opencode/` | `_state/` | model cache and other interface state | | `~/.agents/skills/` | `_agents/` | skills installed with the `skills` CLI | | selected sessions | `_sessions/` | one small compressed file per session, if you [opt in](#sessions) | | your extra paths | `_extra/` | any other file or folder you add, such as `.config/gh/config.yml` | Each part can be switched off under **What to sync**. A part you switch off stays local in both directions: your edits are not sent, and other machines' versions do not replace yours. **Never synced** - The `opencode.db` database itself, tool output, snapshots and logs. Sessions travel as separate small files instead. - `node_modules` and other generated folders. - opencode-sync's own settings and overrides files. - Anything that describes one machine rather than your setup: OpenCode 2's `service.json` (one in the config folder and one in the state folder; each holds the local background service's password), lock files, prompt history, recent-file lists, and `cli.json` plugin entries that point into this machine's home folder. --- ## OpenCode 2 opencode-github-sync 3.3.0 and later support OpenCode 2 (`@opencode/cli`) fully. Machines on OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2 can use one repository side by side. What is different on OpenCode 2, and what this tool does about it: | OpenCode 2 changed | What opencode-sync does | | --- | --- | | Sessions live in new tables, and a fresh OpenCode 2 database has no old ones | Reads and writes OpenCode 2's own tables. OpenCode 1 machines keep their own format; each side imports only its own kind and leaves the other's in place | | `/session` lists only the sessions of the current folder's project | Each imported session is placed in the project OpenCode 2 uses for that folder on the receiving machine, so it appears in `/session` | | Sessions migrated from 1.x can vanish from `/session` | `opencode-sync repair-sessions` moves them back where `/session` looks | | Logins live in the database, and `auth.json` is read at most once | With credential sync on, logins are copied between the two around every sync | | Interface preferences moved to `cli.json` | Shared as part of the main config, without this machine's plugin paths | | A `service.json` with a password sits in the config folder | Never committed, and removed from repositories an older version wrote it into | | Configuration reloads by itself | The "restart OpenCode" hint only appears where a restart is still needed: OpenCode 1, or a changed plugin | To move a machine from OpenCode 1 to 2, see [Upgrading to OpenCode 2](#upgrading-to-opencode-2). --- ## Autosync

When autosync is on, the operating system starts `opencode-sync autosync run` every few minutes and at sign-in (on Windows also when you unlock the screen or reconnect over Remote Desktop). Each run makes one decision: 1. **Is it quiet?** If a file in your config or skills folders changed in the last minute, something is still being written. Sending now could publish a half-saved file, so the push waits. 2. **Can it at least receive?** While you are busy it still takes other machines' changes, but only when this machine has nothing of its own waiting. Otherwise everything waits for the next run. 3. **Push and receive.** Your changes go up and other machines' changes come down in one step. The rules that keep it safe: - **Machines take turns.** Each machine waits a few seconds, fixed per machine, so two machines on the same schedule do not collide every time. If another machine still gets there first, this one takes the new commit and tries again; that does not count as an error. - **It backs off but never gives up.** After three failures in a row (usually no network) it waits 30 minutes, then an hour between attempts. The first success puts it back on schedule. - **It interrupts you twice at most.** One notification when it starts backing off, one when it recovers. Ordinary syncs are silent. - **It never runs twice at once.** One lock is shared by the scheduled job, the command, the menu and every OpenCode window; whoever finds it busy skips. - **It never approves a large change by itself.** Anything that trips the [large-change guard](#safety) is held back and you get a notification. - **It renews a shared ChatGPT login.** See [Credentials](#credentials). | Platform | Scheduler | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | Task Scheduler | Runs hidden. To run while signed out, turn it on in the menu and install from an administrator terminal | | macOS | launchd agent | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.opencode-github-sync.autosync.plist` | | Linux | systemd user timer | Falls back to a crontab line. On a server, run `loginctl enable-linger` so it runs while you are logged out | `opencode-sync autosync status` shows the last run, the last error and the next attempt. With autosync on, the plugin stops pushing on idle so the two never compete; it still pulls when OpenCode starts. --- ## Per-machine overrides Some settings belong to one machine only: a work proxy, a local tool path, an MCP server that only exists on one box. Put them in `~/.config/opencode/opencode-sync.overrides.jsonc`, or use **This machine's overrides** in the menu: ```jsonc { "model": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4", "mcp": { "playwright": { "enabled": true } } } ``` ``` repo opencode.jsonc shared, committed + overrides.jsonc this machine only, never committed ───────────────────────── merged = effective opencode.jsonc what OpenCode reads ``` Objects merge key by key, lists and plain values replace, and `null` removes a key. Before every push, each key the overrides file claims is put back to the repository's value, so your machine-only values never reach other machines. Without an overrides file the config is copied exactly as written, comments and all. --- ## Sessions Off by default. Turn it on only for a private repository: conversations are private. ```bash opencode-sync sessions enable opencode-sync sessions list opencode-sync sessions include ses_065cad1caffeN3lf1RgLZno30 # always sync this one opencode-sync sessions exclude ses_0ba19b4e7ffeMbSmWYi3Nj6xfZ # never sync this one ``` Sessions are not synced by committing the database. A real OpenCode database grows to several gigabytes, mostly tool output, and git cannot merge it. Instead each session is exported on its own as a small compressed file: - **Small.** Only recent sessions travel (7 days and 50 sessions by default), and any single session over 5 MB is skipped. - **Conflicts are rare and resolved.** Two machines working on different sessions touch different files. When one session changed on two machines, the newer copy wins; on OpenCode 2 the replaced local copy is saved to the recovery folder first if it had messages the newer one lacks. - **Never disturbs a running conversation.** A session that is busy on this machine is not replaced, and runtime state (busy, compacting, retry counters) is never carried over, so a receiving machine never resumes a conversation on its own. - **Lands in the right place.** On OpenCode 2 an imported session is placed in the project OpenCode 2 uses for its folder here. A folder under the other machine's home is matched to the same folder under yours; a folder this machine does not have puts the session in your home folder's project. - **Safe to import.** Each session is imported in one transaction, so a failure leaves your database as it was. Window, count and size limits are under **What to sync → Session settings**. Sessions need Node.js 22.5 or newer. **Sessions missing from `/session` after upgrading to OpenCode 2?** OpenCode's own migration leaves some of them in a project `/session` never shows. Their content is intact: ```bash opencode-sync repair-sessions # preview: what would move where opencode-sync repair-sessions --apply # move them ``` --- ## Credentials Off by default, and refused outright when the repository is public. Turn it on under **What to sync → Credentials** or with `"includeCredentials": true`. On OpenCode 1, `auth.json` is synced as a file. On OpenCode 2, which keeps logins in its database, opencode-sync also copies between the database and `auth.json` around every sync: - The account you pick in OpenCode (for example after `/connect` or switching accounts) is what the other machines receive. A running OpenCode picks up an incoming account on its next request, without a restart. - A renewed login updates the existing account instead of adding a copy. When both sides changed, the one that expires later wins. - An account missing from an incoming copy never logs this machine out. Logging out on a machine removes that account from the shared copy. - A broken or half-written `auth.json` is never overwritten. - To tell which side changed, only hashes of the last synced values are kept, in `opencode-sync-credentials.json` next to the database. Never the secrets. **Shared ChatGPT login.** Renewing an OpenAI login invalidates the previous one, so machines that each renew the same login log each other out. With credential sync on, only one machine renews it: the scheduled job claims a lease in the sync repository (an atomic operation on GitHub's side), renews three days before the login expires, and the next sync hands the new login to every other machine. A claim older than 15 minutes is considered abandoned and can be taken over. Set `"openaiRefreshLease": false` to turn this off. --- ## Safety

- **All-or-nothing writes.** Files are written beside their target and then swapped in, so a crash mid-sync cannot leave a half-written config that stops OpenCode from starting. - **Push verification.** After pushing, the remote is read back. `git push` can report success without the remote changing; that is checked, not assumed. - **One sync at a time.** A lock shared by the plugin, the command, the menu and the scheduled job. - **Large-change guard.** A push that adds more than 300 files, more than 10 MB in total, or any single file over 2 MB stops and asks. The limits are adjustable. Generated folders such as `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `dist` and `.cache` are never sent. - **Recovery folder.** Before a forced pull, a "repository wins" first link, a restore from history, or replacing a session that was continued on both machines, what is about to be replaced is copied to `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode-sync-recovery/-/`. - **Machine secrets stay home.** OpenCode 2's `service.json`, lock files and per-machine histories are never committed. - **Your hostname stays private.** Commits name the machine by a stable pseudonym (or a name you choose), never by its real hostname. - **Symlinks are refused, not followed**, so a sync cannot copy files from outside the folders it owns. --- ## The menu Run `opencode-sync` with no arguments.

Arrow keys or the shown hotkey pick an item, space ticks a checkbox, Enter confirms and Esc goes back. When the input is not a terminal (a pipe, a script, CI) every prompt becomes a numbered question, so the menu can be driven from a file. | Item | What you can do there | | --- | --- | | **Sync now** | Push and receive, receive only, push only, or preview first | | **What to sync** | Tick main config, instruction files, agents, commands, plugins, skills, credentials, sessions; set session limits; add extra paths | | **Autosync** | On or off; every 5/10/15/30/60 minutes or your own interval; pause; run while signed out (Windows); notifications | | **Update** | Check npm for a newer version, upgrade, or update automatically once a day | | **This machine's overrides** | Open the overrides file in your editor and see what it changes | | **Diagnostics** | git, node, gh, repository access, the scheduled job, the last log lines; export a support bundle | | **Danger zone** | Make this machine match the repository, or the other way round (type `overwrite` to confirm) | | **Uninstall** | Remove the scheduled job, optionally unlink and remove the command. Your configuration is never deleted | | **Network proxy** | A proxy for git, gh and npm, used only by opencode-sync | | **Restore a file from history** | Pick a file, pick a version, put it back | | **Devices** | Every machine that has synced and when; rename this one | | **Large-change guard** | The limits that make a big push stop and ask | | **Language** | English, 简体中文 or automatic | --- ## OpenCode plugin The plugin is optional. It pulls when OpenCode starts, can push when a session goes idle, and adds an `opencode_sync` tool so you can ask for a sync in plain language. ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["opencode-github-sync"] } ``` The `"plugin"` key works on OpenCode 1.x (1.3.4 and later) and 2.x. If you run only OpenCode 2 you can use its native `"plugins"` key instead, but do not list the plugin under both: OpenCode 2 loads entries from both lists. OpenCode 1.0–1.3.3 cannot load 3.1.0 and later; stay on `opencode-github-sync@3.0.1` there. Keep the command installed even if you use the plugin. A plugin cannot repair a configuration that stops OpenCode from loading it; `opencode-sync pull --force` can. --- ## Commands | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `opencode-sync` | Open the menu (same as `opencode-sync menu`) | | `opencode-sync init [name]` | Create a private sync repository with `gh` | | `opencode-sync link ` | Use an existing repository | | `opencode-sync setup --mode cli\|link\|auto` | Non-interactive setup, used by the installers | | `opencode-sync push` | Send this machine's changes | | `opencode-sync pull` | Take the shared configuration | | `opencode-sync status` | What is in sync and what is not | | `opencode-sync autosync enable` / `disable` | Turn autosync on or off for this machine | | `opencode-sync autosync install` / `uninstall` | Register or remove the scheduled job only | | `opencode-sync autosync status` | Last run, last error, next attempt | | `opencode-sync autosync run` | One scheduled pass, now | | `opencode-sync autosync pause \|tomorrow` / `resume` | Pause or resume | | `opencode-sync autosync reset` | Clear the failure counter | | `opencode-sync sessions list\|enable\|disable` | Session sync | | `opencode-sync sessions include\|exclude ` | Always or never sync one session | | `opencode-sync repair-sessions [--apply]` | OpenCode 2: move sessions missing from `/session` into their project (preview without `--apply`) | | `opencode-sync overrides` | Create or locate the overrides file | | `opencode-sync config` | Print the settings | | Flag | Effect | | --- | --- | | `--force` | Overwrite the other side (asks you to type `yes`; `--yes` skips) | | `--dry-run` | Show what would change, change nothing | | `--allow-large` | Push even when the large-change guard objects | | `--lang en\|zh-CN` | Interface language for this run | | Environment variable | Effect | | --- | --- | | `OPENCODE_SYNC_LANG` | Interface language | | `OPENCODE_SYNC_HOST_ALIAS` | Machine name used in commits | | `OPENCODE_SYNC_PROXY` | Proxy for git, gh and npm | | `OPENCODE_SYNC_VERBOSE=1` | Full file lists and stack traces | | `SYNC_REMOTE_URL` | Override the repository URL | | `NO_COLOR` | Plain output | --- ## Settings file `~/.config/opencode/opencode-sync.jsonc` stays on this machine and is never committed. The menu edits it for you; every key is optional. ```jsonc { "repo": { "owner": "you", "name": "my-opencode-config", "branch": "main" }, "machineAlias": "laptop", "includeCredentials": false, "openaiRefreshLease": true, "includeSkills": true, "includeState": true, "extraPaths": [".config/gh/config.yml"], "categories": { "config": true, "instructions": true, "agents": true, "commands": true, "plugins": true }, "sessions": { "enabled": false, "days": 7, "maxSessions": 50, "maxSessionBytes": 5242880 }, "autosync": { "enabled": false, "intervalMinutes": 5, "settleSeconds": 60, "runWhenLoggedOff": false, "autoUpdate": false }, "guard": { "maxFiles": 300, "maxBytes": 10485760, "maxFileBytes": 2097152 }, "proxy": "", "language": "", "notifications": true, "autoPullOnStartup": true, "autoPushOnIdle": false } ``` | Key | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `machineAlias` | Name for this machine in commits; unset means a stable pseudonym | | `includeCredentials` | Sync logins ([Credentials](#credentials)); private repositories only | | `openaiRefreshLease` | With credentials on, let one machine at a time renew a shared ChatGPT login | | `includeSkills` / `includeState` | Sync `~/.agents/skills` / `~/.local/state/opencode` | | `extraPaths` | Extra files or folders, relative to your home folder | | `categories` | Which parts of the config folder are shared | | `sessions` | [Session](#sessions) window, count and size limits | | `autosync` | [Autosync](#autosync) interval, quiet period, run while signed out, daily self-update | | `guard` | [Large-change guard](#safety) limits | | `autoPullOnStartup` / `autoPushOnIdle` | What the [plugin](#opencode-plugin) does | --- ## Troubleshooting **I am behind a proxy.** Pass `--proxy http://host:port` (or `-Proxy` on Windows) to the installer. It is used for npm and git during the install and saved for later syncs, including the ChatGPT login renewal. Change it any time under **Network proxy**. **`curl | sh` does not ask me anything.** The script itself arrives through the pipe, so it reads your answers from the terminal instead. Where there is no terminal (CI, a Dockerfile) nobody can answer: pass `--mode` and `--repo`, plus `--yes` if Node.js or git may need installing. **Windows says running scripts is disabled.** `irm ... | iex` does not run a script file, so the execution policy does not apply. To run a downloaded `install.ps1` as a file, use `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1`. **`opencode-sync` is not found after installing.** npm installed it into a folder that is not on your `PATH`. `npm prefix -g` shows the folder; add its `bin` (or the folder itself on Windows) to `PATH`. **Autosync is on but nothing happens.** Run `opencode-sync autosync status`. It shows whether it is paused, backing off after errors, or waiting because files are still changing. **Diagnostics** in the menu shows whether the scheduled job is registered. **A synced session does not show up in `/session` (OpenCode 2).** Open OpenCode in the session's folder; `/session` lists only that folder's project. Sessions from before your upgrade to OpenCode 2: run `opencode-sync repair-sessions --apply`. **Sessions are not synced at all.** Check `opencode-sync status` shows session sync as on, and that `node --version` is 22.5 or newer. **A login did not arrive on another machine (OpenCode 2).** Credentials must be on for both machines. Run a sync on the machine where you logged in, then on the other one. If two accounts of one provider are both marked active, nothing is changed for that provider; switch accounts once in OpenCode to settle it. **A pull conflicted with my local edits.** Your edits are kept in a git stash and the exact commands to get them back are printed. Nothing is lost. **"This machine has N commits that were never pushed."** Pulling would throw them away, so it stops. Run `opencode-sync push`, or `pull --force` to discard them. **Authentication failed.** Run `gh auth login -h github.com`. Private repositories need the `repo` scope. **OpenCode will not start after a sync.** This is what the command is for: ```bash opencode-sync pull --force ``` The files it replaces go to the recovery folder first. --- ## Upgrading ### Upgrading to OpenCode 2 Upgrade opencode-github-sync to 3.3.0 or later on every machine first. 3.2.x cannot read OpenCode 2 sessions, and it commits OpenCode 2's `service.json`. 1. Install OpenCode 2. With npm 12 its install scripts must be allowed, or the `opencode` command is only a placeholder: ```bash npm install -g @opencode/cli --allow-scripts=@opencode/cli ``` 2. Optionally stop OpenCode 2 from updating itself in the background; an unattended self-update through npm 12 can break the install: ```bash opencode service set env OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE 1 ``` 3. Start OpenCode 2 once so it migrates your 1.x data, then bring back the sessions `/session` no longer shows: ```bash opencode-sync repair-sessions # preview opencode-sync repair-sessions --apply ``` **If you synced with 3.2.x on OpenCode 2**, your repository may contain `service.json` and `_state/service.json`. 3.3.0 removes them on its next push, but they stay in the repository's history. The password in them only opens the local background service of that machine. To remove them from history as well, delete the repository and push again from one machine. ### Upgrading from 3.1.x or 3.2.x ```bash npm install -g opencode-github-sync@latest ``` Nothing else is required: settings, overrides and the repository keep working, and autosync stays off until you turn it on. If you sync on a timer with a script of your own, remove it before turning autosync on so the two do not compete. If you used `autoPushOnIdle` in the plugin, autosync replaces it on machines where you turn it on. The [changelog](./CHANGELOG.md) lists every change. --- ## Development ```bash npm install npm run check # lint, typecheck and tests npm run build ``` The tests run against real git repositories on disk and simulate several machines, so pushing, pulling, rebasing, autosync scheduling and the menu are exercised end to end. Session and credential tests use the schema of a real OpenCode 2.2.5 database and fake tokens only. Real scheduled jobs are only ever registered on disposable CI runners. --- ## Star history --- ## License [MIT](https://github.com/lazyalex616/opencode-github-sync/blob/main/LICENSE)

If this saved you some time, a ⭐ is appreciated.

--- 你在好几台电脑上用 OpenCode，每台都会慢慢变得不一样：这台加了个智能体，那台多了个 MCP 服务器，笔记本上装的技能台式机上又忘了装。 **opencode-github-sync** 借助一个 GitHub 私有仓库，让所有电脑保持同一套配置。想手动同步就手动，也可以让每天用的电脑在后台自己同步。OpenCode 1 和 OpenCode 2 都支持，两种版本的电脑还能共用同一个仓库。 **能得到什么** - 配置、指令文件、智能体、自定义命令、插件、主题和技能，每台电脑都一样。 - 可选：登录凭据和最近的对话也一起同步。 - 只属于某台电脑的设置，留在那台电脑上。 - 覆盖任何东西之前都会先留一份副本；同步出了问题导致 OpenCode 启动不了，也能用命令行修好。 ## 目录 - [安装](#安装) - [第一次运行](#第一次运行) - [同步哪些内容](#同步哪些内容) - [OpenCode 2](#opencode-2) - 第一次运行 `opencode-sync` 时，它会问你这台电脑打算怎么用： | | 只装命令 | 主力设备 + 自动同步 | | --- | --- | --- | | 怎么同步 | 你自己运行 `opencode-sync push` / `pull`，或者插件在 OpenCode 启动时拉取 | 操作系统每隔几分钟同步一次，OpenCode 没开也照样同步 | | 适合 | 偶尔用一下的电脑、共用或受管控的电脑 | 每天干活用的电脑 | | 后台任务 | 无 | 任务计划程序、launchd 或 systemd 定时器 | 然后关联一个仓库： - **还没有仓库？** 它会用 `gh` 帮你建一个私有仓库（也可以运行 `opencode-sync init`）。 - **已经有了？** 从列表里选，或者填 `用户名/仓库名`、任意 git 地址（也可以运行 `opencode-sync link 用户名/仓库名`）。 如果仓库里已经有内容、本机也有自己的文件，菜单会先列出差异让你选以哪边为准。被替换那一边的文件会先复制到[恢复目录](#安全机制)。 之后随时可以在**自动同步**菜单里改。自动同步按电脑单独开启：在这台打开，不会影响其他任何一台。 --- ## 同步哪些内容

`~/.config/opencode` 文件夹本身就是仓库的工作目录，其他位置的内容会镜像到仓库里的子文件夹。 | 本机位置 | 仓库里的位置 | 内容 | | --- | --- | --- | | `~/.config/opencode/` | 根目录 | `opencode.json(c)`、`tui.json(c)`、OpenCode 2 的 `cli.json`、智能体、自定义命令、插件、主题、指令文件 | | `~/.local/share/opencode/` | `_data/` | 项目信息；[开启后](#登录凭据)还有登录凭据 | | `~/.local/state/opencode/` | `_state/` | 模型缓存等界面状态 | | `~/.agents/skills/` | `_agents/` | 用 `skills` 命令安装的技能 | | 选中的会话 | `_sessions/` | 每个会话一个压缩小文件，需要[开启](#会话同步) | | 额外路径 | `_extra/` | 你自己加的任意文件或文件夹，比如 `.config/gh/config.yml` | 每一项都能在**同步哪些内容**里关掉。关掉的项双向都只留在本机：你的改动不会推上去，别的电脑的版本也不会覆盖你的。 **永远不同步** - `opencode.db` 数据库本身、工具输出、快照和日志。会话改为单独导出成小文件同步。 - `node_modules` 之类的生成目录。 - opencode-sync 自己的设置文件和专属设置文件。 - 只描述某一台电脑、而不是你的配置的东西：OpenCode 2 的 `service.json`（配置目录和状态目录里各一份，里面都有本机后台服务的密码）、锁文件、输入历史、最近文件列表，以及 `cli.json` 里指向本机用户目录的插件条目。 --- ## OpenCode 2 opencode-github-sync 3.3.0 起完整支持 OpenCode 2（`@opencode/cli`）。OpenCode 1 和 OpenCode 2 的电脑可以同时用一个仓库。 OpenCode 2 改了什么，这个工具怎么应对： | OpenCode 2 的变化 | opencode-sync 的做法 | | --- | --- | | 会话存在新的表里，全新的 OpenCode 2 数据库根本没有旧表 | 直接读写 OpenCode 2 自己的表。OpenCode 1 的电脑保留原来的格式；各自只导入自己那一类，不会删掉对方的 | | `/session` 只列出当前文件夹所属项目的会话 | 导入的会话会放进接收方 OpenCode 2 为那个文件夹使用的项目里，所以能在 `/session` 里看到 | | 从 1.x 迁移过来的会话可能在 `/session` 里消失 | `opencode-sync repair-sessions` 把它们移回 `/session` 会看的地方 | | 登录凭据存在数据库里，`auth.json` 最多只读一次 | 开启凭据同步后，每次同步前后都会在两者之间复制 | | 界面偏好搬到了 `cli.json` | 归入主配置一起同步，但去掉本机的插件路径 | | 配置目录里多了一个带密码的 `service.json` | 永远不提交；旧版本提交过的，会从仓库里删掉 | | 配置会自动重新加载 | 只在真正需要时提示重启：OpenCode 1，或者插件有变化 | 把一台电脑从 OpenCode 1 升到 2，请看[升级到 OpenCode 2](#升级到-opencode-2)。 --- ## 自动同步

开启自动同步后，操作系统每隔几分钟、以及每次登录时（Windows 上还包括解锁屏幕和远程桌面重连时）运行一次 `opencode-sync autosync run`。每次运行只做一个判断： 1. **现在安静吗？** 如果配置或技能文件夹里最近一分钟有文件变化，说明还在写入。这时推送可能把写了一半的文件发出去，所以先不推。 2. **至少能接收吗？** 你在忙的时候它照样接收别的电脑的改动，但前提是本机没有自己的改动在等着。否则全部留到下一次。 3. **推送并接收。** 你的改动上传、别的电脑的改动下载，一步完成。 保证安全的规则： - **电脑之间错开时间。** 每台电脑等几秒钟（每台固定），同一时间表的两台不会每次都撞上。别的电脑还是抢先了，这台就接过新提交再试一次，不算出错。 - **会退避，但永不放弃。** 连续失败三次（通常是没网）后等 30 分钟，之后每小时试一次。第一次成功就恢复正常节奏。 - **最多打扰你两次。** 开始退避时通知一次，恢复时通知一次。平常同步不弹任何东西。 - **同一时间只跑一个。** 定时任务、命令行、菜单和每个 OpenCode 窗口共用一把锁，谁发现被占用就跳过。 - **从不自己批准大改动。** 触发[大改动保护](#安全机制)的推送会被拦下，并给你发通知。 - **负责续期共用的 ChatGPT 登录。** 见[登录凭据](#登录凭据)。 | 平台 | 调度方式 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | 任务计划程序 | 隐藏运行。想在注销后也运行，先在菜单里打开，再用管理员终端安装 | | macOS | launchd 代理 | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.opencode-github-sync.autosync.plist` | | Linux | systemd 用户定时器 | 不可用时退回 crontab。服务器上请运行 `loginctl enable-linger`，退出登录后也能运行 | `opencode-sync autosync status` 会显示上次运行、最后的错误和下次尝试时间。开启自动同步后，插件不再在会话空闲时推送，避免两边抢；OpenCode 启动时照样拉取。 --- ## 本机专属设置 有些设置只属于某一台电脑：公司代理、本地工具路径、只在某台电脑上有的 MCP 服务器。把它们写进 `~/.config/opencode/opencode-sync.overrides.jsonc`，或者用菜单里的**本机专属设置**： ```jsonc { "model": "github-copilot/claude-sonnet-4", "mcp": { "playwright": { "enabled": true } } } ``` ``` 仓库里的 opencode.jsonc 共享，会提交 + overrides.jsonc 只在本机，永不提交 ───────────────────────── 合并 = 实际生效的 opencode.jsonc OpenCode 读的就是它 ``` 对象按键逐个合并，列表和普通值直接替换，`null` 表示删除这个键。每次推送前，专属设置里出现过的键都会恢复成仓库里的值，所以只属于本机的值永远不会传到别的电脑。没有专属设置文件时，配置原样复制，注释也保留。 --- ## 会话同步 默认关闭。只在私有仓库里开启：对话内容是隐私。 ```bash opencode-sync sessions enable opencode-sync sessions list opencode-sync sessions include ses_065cad1caffeN3lf1RgLZno30 # 这个会话始终同步 opencode-sync sessions exclude ses_0ba19b4e7ffeMbSmWYi3Nj6xfZ # 这个会话永不同步 ``` 会话不是靠提交整个数据库来同步的。真实的 OpenCode 数据库会涨到好几 GB，大部分是工具输出，git 也没法合并它。所以每个会话单独导出成一个压缩小文件： - **体积小。** 只同步最近的会话（默认 7 天、最多 50 个），单个超过 5 MB 的会话直接跳过。 - **冲突少，而且有处理。** 两台电脑各自处理不同的会话，改的是不同的文件。同一个会话在两台电脑上都有改动时，保留较新的那份；在 OpenCode 2 上，如果本机那份有较新那份没有的消息，会先存进恢复目录再替换。 - **不打扰正在进行的对话。** 本机正在运行的会话不会被替换；运行中的状态（忙碌、压缩中、重试次数）也不会被带过去，所以接收方绝不会自己接着跑一段对话。 - **放到对的地方。** 在 OpenCode 2 上，导入的会话会放进本机 OpenCode 2 为那个文件夹使用的项目里。另一台电脑用户目录下的文件夹，对应到你用户目录下的同名文件夹；本机没有的文件夹，会话放进用户目录的项目里。 - **导入安全。** 每个会话在一个事务里导入，失败了数据库保持原样。 时间范围、数量和大小上限在**同步哪些内容 → 会话同步设置**里调。会话同步需要 Node.js 22.5 或更新版本。 **升级到 OpenCode 2 后，`/session` 里少了会话？** OpenCode 自己迁移时，会把一部分会话留在 `/session` 永远不显示的项目里，内容其实都在： ```bash opencode-sync repair-sessions # 预览：哪些会话会移到哪里 opencode-sync repair-sessions --apply # 真正移动 ``` --- ## 登录凭据 默认关闭，仓库是公开的时候直接拒绝开启。在**同步哪些内容 → 登录凭据**里打开，或者设 `"includeCredentials": true`。 OpenCode 1 上，`auth.json` 作为文件同步。OpenCode 2 把登录存在数据库里，所以 opencode-sync 还会在每次同步前后，在数据库和 `auth.json` 之间复制： - 你在 OpenCode 里选中的账号（比如 `/connect` 之后或者切换账号之后），就是其他电脑收到的账号。正在运行的 OpenCode 下一次请求就会用上收到的账号，不用重启。 - 续期后的登录会更新原来那个账号，不会多出一份。两边都有变化时，以到期更晚的为准。 - 传过来的副本里缺了某个账号，不会把本机登出。在某台电脑上退出登录，会从共享副本里删掉这个账号。 - 损坏或写了一半的 `auth.json` 绝不会被覆盖。 - 判断哪边变了，只保存上次同步值的哈希，放在数据库旁边的 `opencode-sync-credentials.json` 里，从不保存密钥本身。 **共用的 ChatGPT 登录。** 续期 OpenAI 登录会让上一份失效，所以各自续期同一个登录的电脑会互相挤掉。开启凭据同步后，只由一台电脑续期：定时任务先在同步仓库里抢一个“租约”（GitHub 那边保证同一时刻只有一台能抢到），在登录到期前三天续期，下一次同步再把新登录发给其他电脑。超过 15 分钟没完成的租约视为作废，别的电脑可以接手。不想要可以设 `"openaiRefreshLease": false`。 --- ## 安全机制

- **写入要么全成功要么不动。** 文件先写在目标旁边，再一次性换过去。同步到一半崩溃，也不会留下写了一半、导致 OpenCode 启动不了的配置。 - **推送后核实。** 推送完会回读远端确认。`git push` 有时报成功但远端根本没变，这一点会检查，不会想当然。 - **同一时间只跑一个。** 插件、命令行、菜单和定时任务共用一把锁。 - **大改动保护。** 一次推送新增超过 300 个文件、总量超过 10 MB，或有单个文件超过 2 MB，会先停下来问你。上限可调。`node_modules`、`.venv`、`venv`、`__pycache__`、`dist`、`.cache` 这类生成目录永远不会推送。 - **恢复目录。** 强制拉取、首次关联时以仓库为准、从历史恢复文件、替换一个在两台电脑上都继续过的会话之前，即将被替换的内容会先复制到 `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode-sync-recovery/<时间>-<原因>/`。 - **本机密钥不出门。** OpenCode 2 的 `service.json`、锁文件和本机历史记录永远不会提交。 - **不泄露主机名。** 提交里用固定的代号（或你起的名字）标记电脑，不用真实主机名。 - **拒绝符号链接，不跟随**，同步不会顺着链接把别处的文件复制出去。 --- ## 菜单一览 不带参数运行 `opencode-sync`：

方向键或括号里的快捷键选择，空格勾选，回车确认，Esc 返回。如果输入不是终端（管道、脚本、CI），每个问题都会变成编号提问，所以也能用文件驱动整个菜单。 | 菜单项 | 能做什么 | | --- | --- | | **立即同步** | 推送并接收、只接收、只推送，或者先预览 | | **同步哪些内容** | 勾选主配置、指令文件、智能体、自定义命令、插件、技能、登录凭据、会话；设置会话范围；添加额外路径 | | **自动同步** | 开关；选 5/10/15/30/60 分钟或自定义间隔；暂停；注销后也运行（Windows）；桌面通知 | | **更新** | 检查 npm 上的新版本、立即升级、每天自动更新 | | **本机专属设置** | 用编辑器打开专属设置文件，查看它改了哪些值 | | **诊断** | git、node、gh、仓库访问、定时任务、最近的日志；导出排障包 | | **危险操作** | 让本机和仓库完全一致，或者反过来（要输入 `overwrite` 确认） | | **卸载** | 删除定时任务，可选解除关联、删除命令。你的配置文件永远不会被删 | | **网络代理** | git、gh、npm 用的代理，只对 opencode-sync 生效 | | **从历史版本恢复文件** | 选文件、选版本、恢复 | | **设备列表** | 哪些电脑同步过、上次是什么时候，还能给本机改名 | | **大改动保护** | 设置推送多大的改动时要先停下来问你 | | **界面语言** | English、简体中文或自动 | --- ## OpenCode 插件 插件可装可不装。它会在 OpenCode 启动时拉取，可以在会话空闲时推送，还提供一个 `opencode_sync` 工具，直接说一句“同步一下”就行。 ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["opencode-github-sync"] } ``` `"plugin"` 这个键在 OpenCode 1.x（1.3.4 及以上）和 2.x 上都能用。只用 OpenCode 2 的话也可以写在它自己的 `"plugins"` 里，但不要两个键里都写：OpenCode 2 会把两个列表都加载。OpenCode 1.0–1.3.3 无法加载 3.1.0 及以后的版本，请在这些版本上继续使用 `opencode-github-sync@3.0.1`。 就算用了插件，也请保留命令行。插件修不了“导致插件加载不了”的那份配置，`opencode-sync pull --force` 可以。 --- ## 命令速查 | 命令 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `opencode-sync` | 打开菜单（同 `opencode-sync menu`） | | `opencode-sync init [名字]` | 用 `gh` 新建私有同步仓库 | | `opencode-sync link <用户名/仓库名 或 地址>` | 使用已有仓库 | | `opencode-sync setup --mode cli\|link\|auto` | 无交互设置，安装脚本用的就是它 | | `opencode-sync push` | 推送本机的改动 | | `opencode-sync pull` | 拉取共享配置 | | `opencode-sync status` | 查看哪些已同步、哪些没有 | | `opencode-sync autosync enable` / `disable` | 在本机开启或关闭自动同步 | | `opencode-sync autosync install` / `uninstall` | 只注册或删除定时任务 | | `opencode-sync autosync status` | 上次运行、最后的错误、下次尝试 | | `opencode-sync autosync run` | 马上执行一次定时同步 | | `opencode-sync autosync pause <小时数>\|tomorrow` / `resume` | 暂停或恢复 | | `opencode-sync autosync reset` | 清零失败次数 | | `opencode-sync sessions list\|enable\|disable` | 会话同步 | | `opencode-sync sessions include\|exclude ` | 某个会话始终同步或永不同步 | | `opencode-sync repair-sessions [--apply]` | OpenCode 2：把 `/session` 里看不到的会话移回所属项目（不加 `--apply` 只预览） | | `opencode-sync overrides` | 创建或找到专属设置文件 | | `opencode-sync config` | 打印设置 | | 参数 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `--force` | 覆盖另一端（需要输入 `yes` 确认；加 `--yes` 跳过） | | `--dry-run` | 只显示会改什么，不实际改 | | `--allow-large` | 大改动保护反对时也照样推送 | | `--lang en\|zh-CN` | 本次运行的界面语言 | | 环境变量 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `OPENCODE_SYNC_LANG` | 界面语言 | | `OPENCODE_SYNC_HOST_ALIAS` | 提交里用的电脑名字 | | `OPENCODE_SYNC_PROXY` | git、gh、npm 用的代理 | | `OPENCODE_SYNC_VERBOSE=1` | 显示完整文件列表和错误堆栈 | | `SYNC_REMOTE_URL` | 覆盖仓库地址 | | `NO_COLOR` | 不输出颜色 | --- ## 设置文件 `~/.config/opencode/opencode-sync.jsonc` 只留在本机，永远不会提交。菜单会帮你改，所有键都可以省略。 ```jsonc { "repo": { "owner": "you", "name": "my-opencode-config", "branch": "main" }, "machineAlias": "laptop", "includeCredentials": false, "openaiRefreshLease": true, "includeSkills": true, "includeState": true, "extraPaths": [".config/gh/config.yml"], "categories": { "config": true, "instructions": true, "agents": true, "commands": true, "plugins": true }, "sessions": { "enabled": false, "days": 7, "maxSessions": 50, "maxSessionBytes": 5242880 }, "autosync": { "enabled": false, "intervalMinutes": 5, "settleSeconds": 60, "runWhenLoggedOff": false, "autoUpdate": false }, "guard": { "maxFiles": 300, "maxBytes": 10485760, "maxFileBytes": 2097152 }, "proxy": "", "language": "", "notifications": true, "autoPullOnStartup": true, "autoPushOnIdle": false } ``` | 键 | 含义 | | --- | --- | | `machineAlias` | 提交里这台电脑的名字；不填就用一个固定的代号 | | `includeCredentials` | 同步登录凭据（见[登录凭据](#登录凭据)），只限私有仓库 | | `openaiRefreshLease` | 开启凭据同步时，让共用的 ChatGPT 登录同一时间只由一台电脑续期 | | `includeSkills` / `includeState` | 同步 `~/.agents/skills` / `~/.local/state/opencode` | | `extraPaths` | 额外的文件或文件夹，相对于用户目录 | | `categories` | 配置目录里哪些部分要共享 | | `sessions` | [会话同步](#会话同步)的时间范围、数量和大小上限 | | `autosync` | [自动同步](#自动同步)的间隔、安静时长、注销后运行、每日自动更新 | | `guard` | [大改动保护](#安全机制)的上限 | | `autoPullOnStartup` / `autoPushOnIdle` | [插件](#opencode-插件)的行为 | --- ## 常见问题 **我得走代理。** 给安装脚本加 `--proxy http://主机:端口`（Windows 上是 `-Proxy`）。安装时 npm 和 git 都会用它，之后同步也会继续用，包括 ChatGPT 登录续期。随时可以在**网络代理**里改。 **`curl | sh` 怎么不问我问题？** 脚本本身是从管道传进来的，所以它改从终端读你的回答。如果根本没有终端（CI、Dockerfile），就没人可问了：加上 `--mode` 和 `--repo`；可能需要装 Node.js 或 git 的话再加 `--yes`。 **Windows 提示禁止运行脚本。** `irm ... | iex` 不是运行脚本文件，执行策略管不到它。如果你把 `install.ps1` 下载下来当文件运行，请用 `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1`。 **装完找不到 `opencode-sync`。** npm 把它装到了不在 `PATH` 里的文件夹。`npm prefix -g` 能看到是哪个文件夹，把它下面的 `bin`（Windows 上就是这个文件夹本身）加进 `PATH`。 **开了自动同步却没动静。** 运行 `opencode-sync autosync status`，看看是不是被暂停了、出错后在退避，还是因为文件还在变化而在等。菜单里的**诊断**可以看定时任务有没有注册上。 **同步过来的会话在 `/session` 里看不到（OpenCode 2）。** 在那个会话所在的文件夹里打开 OpenCode；`/session` 只列出当前文件夹所属项目的会话。如果是升级到 OpenCode 2 之前的老会话，运行 `opencode-sync repair-sessions --apply`。 **会话完全没同步。** 看看 `opencode-sync status` 里会话同步是不是开着，以及 `node --version` 是不是 22.5 或更新。 **登录没传到另一台电脑（OpenCode 2）。** 两台电脑都要开启凭据同步。先在登录的那台同步一次，再在另一台同步。如果同一个服务有两个账号都被标成“当前使用”，这个服务不会被改动；在 OpenCode 里切换一次账号就能理顺。 **拉取时和本地改动冲突了。** 你的改动保存在 git stash 里，恢复用的命令会直接打印出来。不会丢东西。 **提示“这台电脑有 N 个提交从没推送过”。** 这时拉取会把它们丢掉，所以先停下。运行 `opencode-sync push`，或者用 `pull --force` 放弃它们。 **认证失败。** 运行 `gh auth login -h github.com`。私有仓库需要 `repo` 权限。 **同步之后 OpenCode 启动不了了。** 命令行就是为这种时候准备的： ```bash opencode-sync pull --force ``` 被替换的文件会先存进恢复目录。 --- ## 升级 ### 升级到 OpenCode 2 先在每台电脑上把 opencode-github-sync 升到 3.3.0 或更新。3.2.x 读不了 OpenCode 2 的会话，还会把 OpenCode 2 的 `service.json` 提交上去。 1. 安装 OpenCode 2。npm 12 必须允许它的安装脚本，否则 `opencode` 命令只是个空壳： ```bash npm install -g @opencode/cli --allow-scripts=@opencode/cli ``` 2. 可选：禁止 OpenCode 2 在后台自动更新；通过 npm 12 无人值守自更新可能把安装弄坏： ```bash opencode service set env OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE 1 ``` 3. 先启动一次 OpenCode 2，让它迁移 1.x 的数据，再把 `/session` 里看不到的会话找回来： ```bash opencode-sync repair-sessions # 预览 opencode-sync repair-sessions --apply ``` **如果你在 OpenCode 2 上用 3.2.x 同步过**，仓库里可能有 `service.json` 和 `_state/service.json`。3.3.0 下次推送时会把它们删掉，但它们还留在仓库历史里。里面的密码只能打开那台电脑本地的后台服务。如果也想从历史里清掉，可以删掉仓库，再从一台电脑重新推送。 ### 从 3.1.x 或 3.2.x 升级 ```bash npm install -g opencode-github-sync@latest ``` 不需要别的操作：设置、专属设置和仓库都照常工作，自动同步在你打开之前一直是关的。如果你之前用自己的脚本定时同步，开启自动同步前先把它停掉，免得两边抢。如果你在插件里开了 `autoPushOnIdle`，在开启了自动同步的电脑上由自动同步接替它。完整改动见[更新日志](./CHANGELOG.zh-CN.md)。 --- ## 开发 ```bash npm install npm run check # 代码检查、类型检查和测试 npm run build ``` 测试直接在磁盘上的真实 git 仓库里跑，并模拟多台电脑，推送、拉取、变基、自动同步调度和菜单都端到端覆盖。会话和凭据测试用的是真实 OpenCode 2.2.5 数据库的表结构，令牌全部是假的。真正的定时任务只会在用完即弃的 CI 机器上注册。 --- ##
